title: stale-routing-policy-cache-led-to-incorrect-model-variant-selection-during-sync
creator: Evelyn Park
description: Production incidents observed where requests for Dedicated and Private tenants were routed to incompatible model variants (e.g., 4-bit quantized variant in a region that expects 8-bit) during a routing policy sync window. Symptoms included increased 5xxs from the runtime, sharp latency spikes, and several customer escalations reporting hallucinations and degraded quality. Impact spanned Hosted API and Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 during the policy rollout window. Initial triage points to stale in-memory routing-policy cache not being invalidated atomically when the policy controller partially failed, allowing a previous tenant routing table to briefly match incoming requests and trigger fallback logic that selected wrong model/region/tier. This ticket tracks root cause analysis and fixes.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create two tenants: T-A (primary eu-west-1, model: transformer-x-8b-8bit) and T-B (primary us-east-1, model: transformer-x-8b-4bit).
2) Trigger a policy rollout for T-A that updates routing rules (simulate large changeset).
3) During policy-controller partial failure (inject network timeout between controller and config-store), send high-rate requests for T-A with sequence lengths that hit KV-cache path.

4) Observe runtime logs: routing lookup returns an older policy fragment, fallback comparator matches a route belonging to T-B due to missing tenant lock, runtime attempts to select 4-bit variant in eu-west-1, inference returns model_incompatibility error or 5xx and high latency.
5) Reproduce reliably by running the policy-sync with a delayed apply and concurrent traffic (tested in staging with injected delay).
impact: Multiple paying customers experienced degraded output quality and service errors for a 12-minute window. Error budget impact was ~0.6% for affected routes; two dedicated customers opened priority support tickets and requested root cause and remediation. Latency p95 for affected endpoints doubled, and token costs increased due to retries and fallback to higher-cost variants in other regions.
root_cause: Race condition in policy apply flow: applyRoutingDelta() performs an incremental update to the in-memory routing cache without acquiring a write lock for per-tenant cache entries. If the config-store update partially fails (e.g., controller writes succeeded but metrics-sync failed), the cache swap is not atomic. Combined with a comparator that allowed cross-tenant route matches when tenant_id was unset in the intermediate state, this permitted stale routing fragments to be used. Additionally, fallback comparator prioritization was too permissive and did not validate model variant compatibility (architecture/quantization) before selecting a fallback region/tier.
proposed_fix: 1) Make policy apply atomic: build new routing table off-thread and perform an atomic pointer swap under a per-tenant lock. 2) Harden comparator: require explicit tenant_id match and add model-compatibility checks (architecture/bitwidth) before fallback selection. 3) Add a transactional write to config-store or compensating rollback on partial failures. 4) Add unit/integration tests for partial failure scenarios and add chaos tests in staging that inject controller timeouts.
rollout_plan: Canary rollout to eu-west-1 runtime instances (5% of runtime fleet) with feature flag routing_atomic_swap=true for 2 hours. If green, expand to dedicated fleets in us-east-1 (25% -> 50% -> 100%) over 24 hours. Apply a config-store migration to add per-tenant cache_version field; migration will be safe-read first and then swap once all runtimes report compatibility. Communication: embargoed incident update to affected customers and internal Slack channel #incidents-routes.
verification_steps: Run synthetic traffic for T-A and T-B at production QPS with sequence length distribution sampling the KV cache path.
Monitor error-rate (5xx) and latency (p95) for the canary group; require no >10% regression vs baseline over 2h.
Run targeted fault injection (controller timeout) in canary to ensure atomic apply prevents cross-tenant matches.
Validate model-compatibility gate blocks incompatible variant selection using unit tests and in-staging probes.
postmortem_actions: Add metric + alert: routing-policy-apply-partial-failures (>0) and tenant-mismatch-fallbacks (>0) with pager for SRE at P0.
Ship tests: add integration test harness that simulates controller partial failures and asserts no cross-tenant routing (ENG-31285).
Update runbooks: include steps for forced cache invalidation and safe rollback during policy rollouts.
Customer comms: prepare incident summary and remediation notes for affected customers; schedule 1:1s with two highest-impact customers.
Post-incident review: 2026-03-18 incident retro with Eng, SRE, Product, and Solutions to capture process improvements.
